summary: A. P. Buddhadatta was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a tutor in Pali at Ananda College and was attested as a member of Kalyanavamsa Nikaya in 1923.
A. S. Gadre was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. In 1944, he was attested as Director of Archaeology for Baroda State and its Archaeology Department.

A. S. Ramanatha Ayyar worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (1918–1941), Superintendent at Travancore State's Department of Archaeology (1922), and held a post in Thiruvithamkoor (~1924–1932).

A. V. Williams Jackson worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University and studied at Halle-Wittenberg. At Columbia, he was Adjunct Professor of English Literature (1883–1890) and Professor (1895–1935).
A.-Ferdinand Hérold was an Indologist. He studied at the École Nationale des Chartes from around 1886 to 1890 and earned his Licensié-ès-lettres at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Aalekhya Malladi specializes in religious studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Emory University by 2022 and was appointed Assistant Professor at McGill University in 2023.

Aaron P. Proffitt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Colorado Boulder and earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Micah L. Auerback, later becoming assistant professor at SUNY Albany.
Abaji Vishnu Kathavate was an Indology scholar who succeeded Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).

Abanindranath Tagore worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College and University, and the Government College of Art and Craft (~1890–1894), later holding a post at the University of Calcutta (~1921–1929).

Abdur Rehman is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Peshawar (attested 1988).

Abel Bergaigne was a French scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Armand Hauvette-Besnault. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, the University of Paris, and the Sorbonne, becoming professor in 1885.

Abel Hovelacque was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Honoré-Joseph Chavée. At the École d'Anthropologie, he was appointed Professor of Linguistics in 1876 and became Director in 1891.

Abhijit Mandal works in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He earned an MA from Ramakrishna Mission Vidyamandira (2011–2013) and a Ph.D. from the University of Calcutta (2014–2018), becoming Assistant Professor at Cooch Behar Panchanan Barma University in 2016.
Abhimanyu Rao is an Indologist who studied under Deepak Dabral. He has held a post at Shiv Nadar School.

Abhiraj Rajendra Mishra is an Indologist who studied under Rāmbhadrācārya. He served as head of the Sanskrit department at Himachal Pradesh University, visiting professor at the University of Indonesia, and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Abidin İtil was an Indologist who studied under Walter Ruben and earned his PhD at Ankara University. He taught Sanskrit there from 1936, served as an assistant (1943–1946), and was Professor and Department Head (~1957–1975).
Abigail I. MacBain is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned an MA at McMaster University (attested 2008) and held a post at the University of Edinburgh in 2022.

Abigail Leach was a classicist and Indologist who studied at Radcliffe College, Vassar College, and Leipzig under James Bradstreet Greenough and Charles Rockwell Lanman. She became Head of Greek at Vassar (1889) and President of the Society for Classical Studies (1898–1900).

Abirlal Gangopadhyay is an Indologist. He completed his BA (Hons.) at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute (2013–2016), his MA at Jadavpur University (2016–2018), and his PhD at the University of Hyderabad (2018–2023).

Abraham Anthony Fokker was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University (~1891–1894). He served as a professor at the University of Indonesia and taught Malay at the University of Amsterdam (~1906–1927).
